submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE (0.472%) among the 3 measurements, at Ca0.22 Cu0.54 V0.24. MEGNet puts the V2O5 HSE gap (2.83 eV) above the 2.72 eV photon energy, which points to a Cu-rich vanadate region absorbing more light. The data partly support this: Cu-rich 139 beat mid-Cu 69. But 157, the other Cu-rich point, had more Ca and less V and was much lower.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.377%, lower than 139; V-rich/mid-Cu region.
Measured EQE 0.177%; higher Ca and lower V in the Cu-rich region hurt performance.

consultations.verdict: Support (weakly): MEGNet puts V2O5 at 2.83 eV HSE, just above the 2.72 eV photon energy, so V-rich films absorb poorly. CuO is narrow-gap. So Cu-rich copper vanadate regions (gap about 2 eV) should absorb 455 nm light. Probe the Cu-rich corner first.

Uninformative for ranking: V2O5 is on the hull, which confirms V-rich films will contain stable vanadate or V2O5 phases. Measuring 69 (Cu 0.26, V 0.52) tests the CuV2O6-like mid-Cu region, which is distinct from the Cu-rich point already measured.

Weak support: the PBE gap for V2O5 (1.18 eV, versus 2.83 eV HSE) is underestimated, and the HSE value suggests V-rich regions absorb poorly at 2.72 eV. The measured data agree: Cu-rich 139 gave 0.47% and mid-Cu 69 gave 0.38%. Index 157 moves to lower V and higher Ca within the Cu-rich region and is a top GP-UCB candidate.
